tasks.title: Pure NumPy MPS Data Structure
tasks.description:
Rewrite DistributedMPS to store plain numpy arrays internally instead of quimb Tensor objects.

Current problem: DistributedMPS stores quimb Tensor objects in self.local_tensors and uses tensor.data / tensor.modify() throughout. The spec requires ALL core computation to use plain numpy arrays only.

What to implement:
- Modify DistributedMPS.__init__ so that when given a quimb MPS, it extracts numpy arrays and converts them to the standard 3D convention: shape (chi_left, d, chi_right) for ALL sites (including first/last with chi=1 boundaries).
- self.local_tensors: Dict[int, np.ndarray] stores raw numpy arrays.
- Remove all .data and .modify() calls from the class.
- Keep the quimb MPS constructor parameter but convert immediately to numpy.
- Add a from_numpy_arrays(arrays, comm) classmethod that takes a list of numpy arrays directly.
- The random() classmethod should create arrays using np.random directly (not quimb), with proper bond dimensions: chi_i = min(d^i, d^(L-i), max_bond_dim). Each rank generates only its local tensors using a shared random seed.
- Preserve all existing public methods: has_local_site, get_local_tensor, set_local_tensor, __getitem__, __setitem__, local_sites, exchange_boundaries, left_canonicalize_local, right_canonicalize_local, mixed_canonicalize_local, canonical_form, local_bond_dims, local_norm, normalize, compress_local, gather.
- exchange_boundaries must send/recv raw numpy arrays (not quimb tensors).
- gather() should return a list of numpy arrays on root rank (or optionally reconstruct quimb MPS if quimb is available, but this is not required for core algorithm).

Tensor shape convention:
  All MPS tensors: (chi_left, d, chi_right)
  First site: (1, d, chi_right)
  Last site: (chi_left, d, 1)
  This matches the LocalDMRGOptimizer convention.
acceptance_criteria: DistributedMPS stores np.ndarray (not quimb Tensor) in local_tensors
All tensors have shape (chi_left, d, chi_right) with chi=1 at boundaries
from_numpy_arrays classmethod works without quimb
random() classmethod creates numpy arrays without quimb, only using np.random with shared seed
exchange_boundaries sends/receives raw numpy arrays via MPI
left_canonicalize_local, right_canonicalize_local work with numpy arrays using QR
compress_local works with numpy arrays using SVD
normalize works with numpy arrays via MPI allreduce
gather returns list of numpy arrays on root rank
Constructor still accepts quimb MPS but converts to numpy internally

tasks.title: Pure NumPy MPO Data Structure
tasks.description:
Rewrite DistributedMPO to store plain numpy arrays internally instead of quimb Tensor objects.

Current problem: DistributedMPO stores quimb Tensor objects and uses quimb's SpinHam1D to build Heisenberg MPO. The spec requires core computation to use plain numpy arrays only.

What to implement:
- Modify DistributedMPO.__init__ so that when given a quimb MPO, it extracts numpy arrays and converts to standard 4D convention: shape (m_left, d_in, d_out, m_right).
- self.local_tensors: Dict[int, np.ndarray] stores raw numpy arrays.
- Remove all quimb Tensor wrapping from from_arrays().
- Add heisenberg_numpy(L, J=1.0, comm=None) classmethod that builds Heisenberg XXX MPO using the 5-state automaton representation WITHOUT quimb:
  - States: 0=identity, 1=Sx, 2=Sy, 3=Sz, 4=identity
  - First site: (1, 2, 2, 5), Last site: (5, 2, 2, 1), Bulk: (5, 2, 2, 5)
  - This MPO is already correctly implemented in optimizer.py._build_heisenberg_mpo - extract and reuse that logic.
- Keep the quimb MPO constructor parameter but convert immediately to numpy.
- Keep the heisenberg() classmethod using quimb for backward compatibility but mark as deprecated.
- Preserve all public methods: has_local_site, get_local_tensor, set_local_tensor, __getitem__, __setitem__, local_sites, n_sites, gather, local_bond_dims, boundary methods.
- gather() returns list of numpy arrays on root.

MPO tensor convention:
  All MPO tensors: (m_left, d_in, d_out, m_right)
  First site: (1, d, d, m)
  Last site: (m, d, d, 1)
  This matches LocalDMRGOptimizer convention.

tasks.title: Consolidate and Fix LocalDMRGOptimizer Core
tasks.description:
Consolidate the three optimizer files (optimizer.py, optimizer_fixed.py, optimizer_final.py) into a single, correct, tested LocalDMRGOptimizer in optimizer.py.

Current problem: There are three different optimizer implementations with inconsistent MPO conventions and untested correctness. The main optimizer.py has a different MPO convention in _build_heisenberg_mpo (first site starts operator creation) vs optimizer_fixed.py (first site propagates identity). Only one should exist.

What to implement:
1. Keep optimizer.py as the single implementation. Delete optimizer_fixed.py and optimizer_final.py.
2. The MPO convention in optimizer.py already matches the standard 5-state automaton:
   - First site W[0,:,:,1]=Sx, W[0,:,:,2]=Sy, W[0,:,:,3]=Sz, W[0,:,:,4]=I
   - Last site W[0,:,:,0]=I, W[1,:,:,0]=Sx, W[2,:,:,0]=Sy, W[3,:,:,0]=Sz
   - Bulk: W[0,:,:,0]=I, W[1,:,:,0]=Sx, ... W[4,:,:,1]=Sx, ... W[4,:,:,4]=I
   This is correct for H = sum_i S_i . S_{i+1}.
3. Ensure _convert_quimb_mps correctly handles all quimb tensor shapes.
4. Ensure _convert_quimb_mpo correctly extracts quimb MPO arrays.
5. Make the constructor accept EITHER:
   a. Lists of numpy arrays (primary interface)
   b. quimb MPS/MPO objects (convenience, auto-converts)
6. Verify compute_energy matches quimb's expectation value.
7. Verify the L=8 Heisenberg ground state energy matches -3.374932... to within 1e-6.

Key methods to preserve:
- left_canonicalize_mps, right_canonicalize_mps (module-level)
- build_left_environment, build_right_environment (module-level)
- LocalDMRGOptimizer.__init__, run, compute_energy
- _optimize_bond, sweep_left_to_right, sweep_right_to_left
- effective_hamiltonian_matvec
- build_heisenberg_mpo_numpy, create_random_mps_numpy (module-level utilities)
acceptance_criteria: Only optimizer.py exists (optimizer_fixed.py and optimizer_final.py deleted)
LocalDMRGOptimizer accepts list of numpy arrays directly
LocalDMRGOptimizer accepts quimb objects and converts correctly
L=8 Heisenberg ground state energy matches -3.3749... within 1e-6
L=10 Heisenberg ground state energy matches -4.2581... within 1e-5
compute_energy returns correct variational energy
Convergence within 20 sweeps for bond_dim=32

tasks.title: Environment Building and Caching Module
tasks.description:
Extract environment building logic into a standalone module that can be used by both serial and distributed DMRG.

Currently build_left_environment and build_right_environment are in optimizer.py. For the distributed case, we need environments that can be built incrementally for a LOCAL subset of sites, and can accept boundary environments received from neighboring MPI ranks.

What to implement in src/distributed/environments.py:

1. build_left_environment(mps, mpo, left_env, site) - same as current but standalone
2. build_right_environment(mps, mpo, right_env, site) - same as current but standalone
3. build_all_left_environments(mps, mpo) -> List[np.ndarray]
   - Builds environments for all sites left-to-right
   - left_envs[0] = ones((1,1,1)), left_envs[i] = env left of site i
4. build_all_right_environments(mps, mpo) -> List[np.ndarray]
   - Builds environments for all sites right-to-left
   - right_envs[L-1] = ones((1,1,1)), right_envs[i] = env right of site i
5. build_local_environments(mps_local, mpo_local, left_boundary_env, right_boundary_env)
   - For distributed case: given local MPS/MPO arrays and boundary environments from neighbors,
     builds all environments within the local partition.
   - left_boundary_env: (chi_bra, m, chi_ket) environment received from left neighbor
   - right_boundary_env: same from right neighbor
   - Returns (left_envs, right_envs) for local sites only.

All functions work with plain numpy arrays. Index conventions:
  MPS: (chi_left, d, chi_right)
  MPO: (m_left, d_in, d_out, m_right)
  Environment: (chi_bra, m_mpo, chi_ket)

build_all_right_environments builds correct chain of environments

tasks.title: MPI Boundary Environment Exchange Protocol
tasks.description:
Implement the MPI communication protocol for exchanging environment tensors between neighboring ranks in the distributed DMRG.

In PDMRG, after each rank optimizes its local sites, it needs to send updated boundary environments to neighbors. This is more complex than just exchanging MPS boundary tensors - we need to exchange the full (chi_bra, m_mpo, chi_ket) environment tensors.

What to implement in src/distributed/mpi_comm.py:

1. exchange_boundary_environments(comm, rank, size, left_env, right_env):
   - Sends left_env to left neighbor, receives right_env from right neighbor
   - Sends right_env to right neighbor, receives left_env from left neighbor
   - Uses Sendrecv to avoid deadlocks
   - Handles variable-sized tensors (bond dims may differ across ranks)
   - Returns (received_left_env, received_right_env)
   - None for boundaries that don't exist (rank 0 left, rank P-1 right)

2. exchange_mps_boundaries(comm, rank, size, local_mps, local_start, local_end):
   - Sends boundary MPS tensors to neighbors
   - Left neighbor gets our leftmost tensor, right neighbor gets our rightmost
   - Returns (left_boundary_tensor, right_boundary_tensor)
   - Used for initializing environments at partition boundaries

3. allreduce_energy(comm, local_energy):
   - Computes global energy via MPI.Allreduce
   - For PDMRG: local energies are from separate partitions, need proper accounting

4. broadcast_convergence(comm, converged, root=0):
   - Broadcast convergence decision from root to all ranks

5. gather_mps_arrays(comm, local_tensors, local_start, local_end, L, root=0):
   - Gather all local MPS numpy arrays to root rank
   - Returns full list of L numpy arrays on root, None on others

All functions work with plain numpy arrays. Handle edge cases:
- Single rank (size=1): no communication needed
- Variable tensor sizes between ranks
- First/last rank boundary conditions
acceptance_criteria: Module src/distributed/mpi_comm.py exists
exchange_boundary_environments handles variable-size tensors
exchange_mps_boundaries sends correct boundary tensors
allreduce_energy sums local energies correctly
broadcast_convergence works for both True and False
gather_mps_arrays reconstructs full MPS on root
All functions handle single-rank case (no MPI communication needed)
All functions use plain numpy arrays
Deadlock-free communication using Sendrecv

tasks.title: Local DMRG Sweep for Partition Subsystem
tasks.description:
Implement a function that runs DMRG sweeps on a LOCAL partition of the MPS/MPO, given boundary environments from neighboring ranks.

This is the core computational kernel of distributed DMRG: each rank takes its local MPS tensors, local MPO tensors, and boundary environments, then performs two-site DMRG sweeps ONLY on its local sites.

What to implement in src/distributed/local_sweep.py:

1. local_dmrg_sweep(local_mps, local_mpo, left_boundary_env, right_boundary_env, bond_dim, n_local_sweeps=2, direction='right'):
   - local_mps: list of numpy arrays for this rank's sites
   - local_mpo: list of numpy arrays for this rank's sites
   - left_boundary_env: (chi_bra, m, chi_ket) from left neighbor, or ones((1,1,1)) for rank 0
   - right_boundary_env: from right neighbor, or ones((1,1,1)) for last rank
   - Performs n_local_sweeps of two-site optimization on local sites
   - Uses the effective Hamiltonian matvec from LocalDMRGOptimizer
   - Updates local_mps in-place
   - Returns: (updated_local_mps, local_energy, updated_left_env, updated_right_env)
   - updated_left_env: environment at right edge of partition (to send to right neighbor)
   - updated_right_env: environment at left edge of partition (to send to left neighbor)

2. compute_local_energy(local_mps, local_mpo, left_boundary_env, right_boundary_env):
   - Compute energy contribution from this partition
   - Uses <psi_local|H_local|psi_local> with boundary environments

Key considerations:
- For partitions with < 2 sites, skip optimization but still compute energy
- Bond truncation via SVD after each two-site optimization
- Left-canonicalize before sweeping right, right-canonicalize before sweeping left
- Build local environments incrementally during sweep (reuse from environments.py)
acceptance_criteria: local_dmrg_sweep optimizes local partition and returns updated MPS
Energy decreases monotonically during local sweeps
Updated boundary environments are correct for passing to neighbors
compute_local_energy gives correct energy for local partition
Handles edge case of 2-site partition
Uses pure numpy/scipy only (no quimb)
SVD truncation respects bond_dim limit

tasks.title: Distributed PDMRG Algorithm - Core Loop
tasks.description:
Rewrite DistributedPDMRG to use the real local DMRG sweep instead of fake energy estimates.

Current problem: The existing pdmrg.py has placeholder logic that returns fake energies like `-0.45 * local_bonds`. This is NOT real DMRG optimization. The _parallel_sweep_half method just calls compute_energy() without any actual optimization.

What to implement (rewrite src/distributed/pdmrg.py):

1. DistributedPDMRG.__init__(L, bond_dim, phys_dim, comm, verbose, mpo_arrays):
   - Creates DistributedMPS using random numpy arrays (no quimb)
   - Creates DistributedMPO using heisenberg_numpy or from_arrays (no quimb)
   - Each rank stores only its local partition
   - Initializes boundary environments as identity tensors

2. solve(n_sweeps, bond_dim, tol) -> float:
   Main PDMRG loop (Stoudenmire-White algorithm):
   a. Initialize: left-canonicalize local MPS, build local environments
   b. For each sweep:
      i.  Each rank runs local_dmrg_sweep on its partition
      ii. Exchange updated boundary environments with neighbors via MPI
      iii. Update local boundary environments from received data
      iv. Compute global energy: each rank computes local energy,
          then allreduce to get total. For non-overlapping partitions,
          we need to account for inter-partition bond energies.
      v.  Check convergence: rank 0 decides, broadcasts to all
      vi. If converged, break

3. _compute_global_energy():
   - Each rank computes <psi_local|H_local|psi_local> using local environments

- Even ranks sweep right while odd ranks sweep left (odd/even decomposition)
- After half-sweep, exchange boundary environments (not just tensors)
- Each rank's local Hamiltonian includes the MPO sites it owns
- Cross-boundary bonds handled by environment exchange

tasks.title: Overlapping Partition Manager for A2DMRG
tasks.description:
Implement the overlapping subdomain partitioning and blending logic for A2DMRG.

A2DMRG differs from PDMRG by using OVERLAPPING subdomains. This task implements the partition management, overlap weight computation, and tensor blending for overlap regions.

What to implement in src/distributed/overlap.py:

1. compute_overlapping_partitions(L, num_ranks, overlap):
   - Returns list of (start, end) tuples for each rank
   - Core regions are disjoint (same as PDMRG partition_sites)
   - Each rank extends by `overlap` sites into neighbors' core regions
   - First rank: no left extension
   - Last rank: no right extension
   - Example: L=20, ranks=4, overlap=2:
     Rank 0: [0, 7), Rank 1: [3, 12), Rank 2: [8, 17), Rank 3: [13, 20)

2. compute_overlap_weights(site, partitions):
   - Returns dict mapping rank -> weight for this site
   - Sites in non-overlapping regions: weight 1.0 for owning rank
   - Sites in overlap regions: linear blend based on distance from partition center
   - Weights sum to 1.0 for each site

3. blend_overlap_tensors(comm, local_tensors, partitions, rank):
   - For each site in an overlap region:
     a. Gather the tensor versions from all ranks that own this site
     b. Compute weighted average using overlap_weights
     c. Update local tensor with blended result
   - Communication: use allgather for overlap region tensors
   - Returns updated local_tensors dict

4. get_core_region(rank, partitions, overlap):
   - Returns (core_start, core_end) for this rank's non-overlapping core
   - Core region = partition minus overlap zones

5. get_overlap_sites(rank, partitions):
   - Returns (left_overlap_sites, right_overlap_sites) lists
   - Sites that overlap with left and right neighbors respectively
acceptance_criteria: compute_overlapping_partitions gives correct overlapping ranges
Overlap regions extend by exactly `overlap` sites into neighbors
compute_overlap_weights returns weights summing to 1.0 for each site
Non-overlap sites have weight 1.0 for their owning rank
blend_overlap_tensors correctly averages tensors in overlap regions
get_core_region returns disjoint non-overlapping core for each rank
Works for edge cases: overlap=0, overlap > partition_size, 1 rank

tasks.title: Coarse Space Correction for A2DMRG
tasks.description:
Implement the coarse space correction from the A2DMRG paper (arXiv:2505.23429).

The current implementation has placeholder logic that adds random noise as 'correction'. This needs to be replaced with the actual two-level method.

What to implement in src/distributed/coarse_space.py:

1. CoarseSpaceSolver class:
   - __init__(L, num_ranks, partitions, bond_dim_coarse=8):
     - Creates a small coarse MPS/MPO representation
     - Coarse space is built from boundary tensors of each subdomain

2. build_coarse_problem(boundary_envs, local_energies):
   - Takes boundary environments from all ranks (gathered)
   - Constructs a reduced Hamiltonian that captures inter-subdomain coupling
   - The coarse space consists of boundary bonds between subdomains
   - Dimension: num_bonds_between_ranks * bond_dim

3. solve_coarse_correction(coarse_hamiltonian) -> List[np.ndarray]:
   - Solve the coarse eigenvalue problem (small, done on all ranks or just root)
   - Returns correction tensors for each boundary

4. apply_coarse_correction(local_mps, corrections, rank, partitions):
   - Modify boundary tensors of local_mps to incorporate the coarse correction
   - Correction is applied additively with a small step size
   - Returns updated local_mps

The coarse correction is the key innovation of A2DMRG over PDMRG:
- PDMRG struggles with global information propagation
- The coarse space provides a 'highway' for global information
- Think of it as: local DMRG fixes local details, coarse correction fixes global correlations

Simplified version (acceptable for first implementation):
- Coarse space = boundary bond tensors from each subdomain
- Coarse Hamiltonian = effective H acting on boundary bonds
- Correction = difference between coarse solution and current boundary values
acceptance_criteria: CoarseSpaceSolver constructs coarse problem from boundary environments
Coarse Hamiltonian is symmetric (Hermitian)
solve_coarse_correction returns meaningful correction tensors
apply_coarse_correction modifies boundary tensors correctly
Correction preserves MPS normalization (approximately)
All operations use pure numpy/scipy

tasks.title: Distributed A2DMRG Algorithm - Core Loop
tasks.description:
Rewrite DistributedA2DMRG to use real DMRG optimization with overlapping subdomains and coarse correction.

Current problem: The existing a2dmrg.py has placeholder logic that normalizes tensors with random perturbations and estimates energy as `-1.4 * (num_tensors - 1)`. This is NOT real DMRG.

What to implement (rewrite src/distributed/a2dmrg.py):

1. DistributedA2DMRG.__init__(L, overlap, bond_dim, comm, ...):
   - Uses compute_overlapping_partitions for subdomain layout
   - Creates DistributedMPS with overlapping regions stored on multiple ranks
   - Creates DistributedMPO (each rank gets its full overlapping portion)
   - No quimb in core

2. solve(n_sweeps, tol) -> A2DMRGResult:
   Main A2DMRG loop:
   a. Initialize: canonicalize local MPS, build local environments
   b. For each global sweep:
      i.   Each rank runs local_dmrg_sweep on its overlapping subdomain
      ii.  Gather boundary environments from all ranks
      iii. Solve coarse correction on root (or all ranks)
      iv.  Broadcast correction, apply to local MPS
      v.   Blend overlap regions: weighted average of tensors in overlap zones
      vi.  Compute global energy (sum local energies, accounting for overlaps)
      vii. Check convergence

3. _blend_overlap_regions():
   - For each site in an overlap zone:
     a. allgather tensor from all ranks that own this site
     b. Compute weighted average using overlap weights
     c. Update local tensor

4. _compute_global_energy():
   - Each rank computes local energy for its CORE region only (not overlap)
   - Allreduce to sum
   - This avoids double-counting energy in overlap regions

5. A2DMRGResult dataclass (keep existing):
   - energy, converged, num_sweeps, wall_time, speedup, efficiency, etc.
